title: Bounded signed total realization with a supplied one-sided flat factor
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the universe of module sheaves [def-weil-size-convention], and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on it. Use the abelian category $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], integer-indexed cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and cochain localization $Q_R:\operatorname{Ch}(R)\to D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Equip $D(R)$ with the K-flat derived tensor and its two-sided representative comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Let $r\le s$ and $u\le v$ be integers. Let $B\in D(R)$ satisfy $H^j(B)=0$ for $j\notin[r,s]$. Let $P^\bullet$ be a given K-flat complex [def-pc-kflat-complex] whose terms are flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and vanish outside $[u,v]$.
There exists a complex $B^\bullet$ with $B^j=0$ for $j\notin[r,s]$ and an isomorphism $B\cong Q_R(B^\bullet)$. For every such representative and representing isomorphism, the right-factor one-sided comparison normalized by the specified two-sided comparison gives an isomorphism in $D(R)$
$$B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q_R(P^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_R\operatorname{Tot}(B^\bullet\otimes_R P^\bullet).$$
The total is the signed direct-sum total complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], with degree-$d$ term $\bigoplus_{j+h=d}B^j\otimes_RP^h$ and differential $d_B\otimes1+(-1)^j1\otimes d_P$ on bidegree $(j,h)$. Its terms vanish for $d\notin[r+u,s+v]$, and each degree has only finitely many potentially nonzero summands. Consequently the displayed derived tensor has zero cohomology outside $[r+u,s+v]$, so belongs to $D^b(\operatorname{Mod}(R))\subset D^+(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. These are vanishing bounds, with no assertion of nonvanishing at either endpoint. No termwise flatness, K-flatness, or finite Tor amplitude of $B$ or $B^\bullet$ is assumed, and $r=s$, $u=v$, zero inputs and the zero ring are allowed.

proof.text: By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the size hypothesis makes $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ abelian. Apply [lem-sfb-bounded-representative] to this abelian category, $B$, and the integers $r\le s$. Its hypotheses are precisely the assumed cohomology vanishings. Obtain $B^\bullet$ with terms zero outside $[r,s]$ and an isomorphism $e:B\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_RB^\bullet$.

Apply the right-factor natural comparison clause of [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated] to the supplied flat-term K-flat complex P. It directly gives a natural isomorphism cR from Q Tot(- tensor P) to D(-,QP), with cR(V) equal to the specified representativeIso(V,P) for every flat-term K-flat V. For every bounded representative K and every e:B ≅ QK, compose D(-,QP).mapIso(e) with cR(K) inverse. This is exactly the required displayed isomorphism; no flatness condition on K is used.

proof.text: The total is the signed direct-sum total of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The tensor functors of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] are additive, so map_isZero shows a tensor summand is zero whenever either input term is zero. For j+h=d outside [r+u,s+v], integer arithmetic shows j<r or s<j or h<u or v<h. Every summand is therefore zero. HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor.hom_ext applied to the identity and zero morphisms makes the degree-d total term zero. Any nonzero summand has (j,h) in the finite product interval [(r,u),(s,v)] in the componentwise order; Set.finite_Icc and subset give the required finiteness in every degree.

proof.text: By ShortComplex.isZero_homology_of_isZero_X₂, the zero degree-d total term has zero degree-d homology. Compose homologyFunctor.mapIso of the comparison for the chosen bounded representative with homologyFunctorFactors from [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; IsZero.of_iso transfers vanishing to the derived tensor. DerivedCategory.isGE_iff and isLE_iff supply its lower bound r+u and upper bound s+v. The existential definitions of plus, minus and bounded in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories] give membership in D^b and D^+. The argument uses no nonzero endpoint assumption, and includes equal endpoints, zero inputs and the zero ring.

lean.statement: theorem bounded_one_sided_tensor_realization {C : Type c} [Category.{m} C] [EssentiallySmall.{a} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C} (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{a}) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (Modules R)] (r s u v : ℤ) (hrs : r ≤ s) (huv : u ≤ v) (B : DerivedCategory (Modules R)) (hB : ∀ j : ℤ, j < r ∨ s < j → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules R) j).obj B)) (P : CochainComplex (Modules R) ℤ) (hP : CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients P) (hPf : ∀ h : ℤ, IsFlatOnSite (J := J) (R := R) (P.X h)) (hPs : ∀ h : ℤ, h < u ∨ v < h → IsZero (P.X h)) : (∃ K : CochainComplex (Modules R) ℤ, (∀ j : ℤ, j < r ∨ s < j → IsZero (K.X j)) ∧ Nonempty (B ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)) ∧ (∃ cR : (totalTensor R).flip.obj P ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ≅ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ (derivedTensor R).flip.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P), (∀ (V : CochainComplex (Modules R) ℤ) (hV : CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients V) (hVf : ∀ j : ℤ, IsFlatOnSite (J := J) (R := R) (V.X j)), cR.app V = representativeIso R V P hV hP hVf hPf) ∧ (∀ (K : CochainComplex (Modules R) ℤ) (_hK : ∀ j : ℤ, j < r ∨ s < j → IsZero (K.X j)) (e : B ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj K), (∃ i : ((derivedTensor R).flip.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)).obj B ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (((totalTensor R).obj K).obj P), i = ((derivedTensor R).flip.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)).mapIso e ≪≫ (cR.app K).symm) ∧ (∀ d : ℤ, d < r + u ∨ s + v < d → IsZero ((((totalTensor R).obj K).obj P).X d)) ∧ (∀ d : ℤ, Set.Finite {p : ℤ × ℤ | p.1 + p.2 = d ∧ ¬ IsZero (((ordinaryTensor R).obj (K.X p.1)).obj (P.X p.2))}))) ∧ (∀ d : ℤ, d < r + u ∨ s + v < d → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules R) d).obj (((derivedTensor R).flip.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)).obj B))) ∧ DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.bounded (((derivedTensor R).flip.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)).obj B) ∧ DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.plus (((derivedTensor R).flip.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)).obj B)
